Hi Julie — I’m looking into the issuance logs now. A couple of notes from past incidents: there’s a race condition where the frontend shows the promo success before the backend transaction completes; in those cases the grant can be queued but not committed.

I’m checking the grant queue and the transaction table for ATL-992. If the auto-grant failed I can push a manual credit and provide a PDF receipt plus an audit link.

Can you attach the screenshot and I’ll correlate with the transaction id?

(Internal) Sofia/Marissa: if this is a manual grant I’ll use the 1-time promo bucket for PLG signups and log it under deal DH-9271. I’ll also note if this is a systemic issue to create a ticket against the grant worker.

Julie — quick update and resolution.

What happened: the PLG promo webhook succeeded on the frontend but the backend grant worker experienced a transient DB deadlock for ATL-992 which prevented the commit. Dev flagged the failure and I performed a manual grant from Growth Ops today.

Actions taken:
- Manual grant of $1,200 trial credits applied to Org ATL-992 (grant id: G-7F9B3).
- Extended trial window by 7 days to ensure you have time for the POC.
- Uploaded an audit receipt: grant_receipt_AtlasHealth.pdf (attached).
- Audit link: https://console.redwood.ai/audit/transactions/7f9b3

Julie — please confirm you now see the $1,200 in the org wallet. Marissa — I’ve flagged this flow for a root-cause ticket (internal) and suggested a guard to prevent frontend success before backend commit. Dev, if you can log SUP-1284 with the grant worker traces that would be great.

Apologies for the hiccup and thanks for your patience.

— Sofia
